newsitem.title: UK: Russia eyes jumbo mark bond for early 1997 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: Russia eyes jumbo mark bond for early 1997 - dealers.

text.p: Russia's plans to issue a mark Eurobond were firming up, with a jumbo transaction expected to surface in February, syndicate managers said on Wednesday.
A deal for around 1.0 billion marks at five years was likely, and some traders said a mandate would soon be awarded for the deal, expected to be launch in early February.

"Russia is expected to make the mandate public soon," said a syndicate manager at a European bank in London. "I expect they will issue a jumbo mark bond, at five years, and it could surface in the first week of February."
A syndicate manager at a German bank in Frankfurt said "There is nothing scheduled so far, but a lot of banks are in touch with Russia and are giving indications to them.
"I would guess the deal would be for between 500 million and 1.0 billion marks at around a five-year maturity," he said.
Russia issued its first international bond since the 1917 revolution in November. The $1.0 billion five-year deal was priced to yield 345 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes.
Russia was expected to issue $1.0 - $2.0 billion in the Eurobond market in 1997, although one Moscow-based trader said the amount could be as high as $3.0 billion.
Syndicate managers said a mark Eurobond would be priced relative to Russia's outstanding dollar transaction.
"If it is a five year it will trade relative to its recent dollar deal, in the 350 basis points region over Bunds," an emerging markets syndicate manager at a European bank said.
"I don't see a very strong case of being much tighter than that, perhaps just a bit tighter," he said.
J.P. Morgan and SBC Warburg were joint lead managers on Russia's dollar debut bond.
A German house, like Commerzbank, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell or Dresdner, was expected to be one of the lead managers on a mark bond, together with a European or U.S. investment bank.
In addition to a mark transaction, dealers said Russia was also eyeing another jumbo dollar deal, also for the first quarter of 1997.
